## Summary

The pivot from research to product: he will **share the source code of 900+ strategies with his War Room** (paid community), built on the Substack Alpha research tracked in this series. The goal: **60+ uncorrelated DARWINs** run by/for members, forming the **Darwinex Tribe with the highest AuM**.

The economics pitch — "this isn't your average prop firm": on Darwinex **you make money when your members reach Gold** (provider-tier economics), and contributors of uncorrelated alpha sources get rewarded. He's considering additional rewards for the highest-ranked members: "a meritocracy where performance, research, and contributions are rewarded… This is how you build the best trading community in the world."

The three photos are the research receipts — six classic institutional strategies, each shown twice: the paper's version vs a **Darwinex-implementable version** (his color code: amber = author's own data, green = what you could trade on Darwinex, grey dashed = SPY for scale; "our offline numbers", not QuantConnect-checked, "not one is a portfolio number"):

| Strategy | Paper's version (costs as labeled) | Darwinex version | Read |
|---|---|---|---|
| AQR 12-mo trend | futures, after costs, Sharpe 1.20 (author 1.17), maxDD 24%, 15.2%/yr | 100 ETFs L/S: 0.32, 36%, ~3.3%/yr | collapses in ETF form, but zero SPY link |
| Winton slow trend | futures, before costs, 0.93 (author 0.81), 22%, ~9.9%/yr | 100 ETFs L/S: 0.45, 14%, 2.9%/yr | less than half |
| Research Affiliates fast+slow | futures, before costs, 0.61 (author 0.80), 17%, 3.8%/yr | 100 ETFs long-only: 0.66, 14%, 4.9%/yr | holds; "no better than plain 12-mo trend, only smoother" |
| ReSolve top-5 momentum | author's 10 ETFs: 1.19 (author claims 1.6), 24%, 10.8%/yr | 100 ETFs long-only: 0.65, 27%, 6.5%/yr | weaker than paper says, halved on Darwinex |
| AQR risk parity | 4 asset classes (US ETFs): 0.96 (author 0.61), 17%, 5.8%/yr | SPY+TLT: 0.79, 30%, 7.5%/yr | "a calm core holding, not an edge: 0.54 corr to SPY" |
| Man Group delayed rebalance | plain 60/40 monthly: 0.83, 31%, 8.7%/yr | Man's rule on SPY+TLT: 0.84 (author 0.96), 28%, 8.3%/yr | "the two lines sit on top of each other — the rule changes almost nothing" |

(SPY benchmark 0.55–0.66 Sharpe / 55% maxDD across the differing panel windows. OCR-approximate; source images preserved.)

## Why it matters

- The series arc completes: replication infrastructure → verification gates → community/product. The photos answer "why Darwinex": every strategy is already measured in Darwinex-implementable form, and the survivors worth owning are the ones with **low SPY correlation** — exactly the raw material a 60-DARWIN uncorrelated tribe needs.
- The panel pattern is honest and useful: **trend strategies keep their diversification but lose 40–70% of Sharpe in Darwinex ETF form; balanced/risk-parity shapes hold Sharpe but are 0.54-correlated "calm cores, not edges."** The scarce commodity is *uncorrelated AND implementable* — a tighter filter than the tweet's marketing admits.
- Incentive alignment is real but circular: the leader earns when members reach Gold, so recruitment is monetized — standard community-operator economics dressed as meritocracy. Nothing wrong, but read the "900 strategies" as the fleet whose **median in-sample Sharpe was ~0.9 costs-in before the robustness gate was ever shown** (still unshown as of [[2026-11-09-zenomtrader-verified-only-costs-sharpe]]).
- **Skepticism gates:** 60 "uncorrelated" DARWINs mined from one corpus is a multiple-testing machine — the DSR/PBO haircut from [[2026-10-28-margincall4-overfitting-validation-dsr-pbo-walkforward]] applies to the fleet, not each row. "900+ strategies" is a fleet count, not a quality count. The Gold-reward claim wasn't quantified (rates, tiers). Offline numbers, author-labeled, no third-party verification — same receipts gap this series always had, in contrast to [[2026-11-09-milk-man-po10-extreme-full-receipts]].
- Actionable in one narrow sense: the 900-strategy code drop is members-only and imminent — join-or-not is a time-boxed decision, filed to Inbox.
